missing_pieces.duty: ED26-BM-RAT2021-4-1-C05 (partial): The component must account for every promised proof or evidence claim in the selected extent and fix the finite dependent-source set; empirical claims must keep their study/task/population/uncertainty and conflict boundaries. The fixed set is tab:p15-w02b-p15-022-dependent-sources, rows D1-D21 with D5a and D8a. Its stated scope (022 lines 668-670 and 848-849) is limited to claims the survey reports as established elsewhere, which is narrower than every claim in the extent. Two kinds of claim are not accounted for anywhere on the route. (i) The survey's own empirical and historical evidence claims: that the Brier score is used in practice to score weather forecasters and political analysts (p. 242); that Lewis's 1994 formulation is how the Principal Principle is usually understood and that the literature overlooks the change of formulation (p. 243); and that formal epistemology is a leading growth area in which Bayesian approaches dominate (p. 247). These are omitted rather than given an evidential status, so none keeps a study/task/population/uncertainty or conflict boundary. (ii) The claim at rationality-4-1.tex lines 216-222, that the accuracy argument needs one specific strictly proper measure, depends on Bronfman (manuscript), cited on p. 242 and listed on p. 249. Bronfman is missing from the fixed dependent-source set.

ED26-METHOD-maximum-entropy-C03 (partial): Normalization and the multiplier equations are explained without presupposing a feasible optimizer (043 lines 103-153 and 296-345), and the worked distributions solve their declared problems. The component's required extent, however, is the complete construction in the original paper including its constraint and normalization derivations, and two of Jaynes's multiplier derivations are absent. (a) Jaynes's (2-15) (p. 623), the maximum-entropy estimate of the parameter derivatives of the constraint functions, equal to -(1/lambda_r) times the parameter derivative of ln Z, is not stated or derived. The forces in (3-4) rest on it. (b) Jaynes's (5-1)-(5-3) (p. 627) are absent: they make lambda_k the integrating factor of the generalized heat dQ_k and the quantity statistically conjugate to f_k, and (5-8) (p. 628) gives lambda = dS/d<E> = 1/T. Neither 166.6 nor 166.7 states, under the hypotheses of thm:p15-w02b-p15-043-existence, how the maximal entropy v_nu(c) changes with the declared values. So the source's interpretation of the multipliers is neither given nor made conditional on its premises. Only the identification lambda_1 = 1/kT appears (043 line 484).

ED26-METHOD-maximum-entropy-C04 (partial): The inferential interpretation is made conditional on the reconstructed premises (J1)-(J5) (043 lines 401-479). Those are not the paper's complete inferential argument and stated premises, which the component's required extent demands. Neither 166.6 nor 166.7 mentions ergodicity, metric transitivity or equal a priori probabilities. Missing: (a) the paper's thesis that statistical mechanics, read as inference, needs no ergodicity, metric transitivity or equal a priori probabilities (pp. 620, 621, 627, 629). Also missing are its premise that the laws of motion add no information about the state beyond what measurement supplied, and its argument that new integrals of motion, or proof that a system is not metrically transitive, would give no rational basis for excluding states the information allows unless new data are added (pp. 624-625). (b) The normative claim that maximum-entropy estimates are justified independently of experimental verification and remain the best estimates the information permits, whether or not they agree with experiment (pp. 620, 626). The interpretation is therefore conditional on an incomplete statement of the source's premises.

units.title: Measurement uncertainty and propagation through an inference

required_components.description: Specify the measurand and measurement equation; distinguish error, correction and uncertainty.
required_components.success_condition: Give an explicit quantity, units, input roles and uncertain corrections.
required_components.failure_condition: Treat uncertainty as an observed error or the standard deviation as every source of uncertainty.

required_components.description: Derive covariance propagation and state the first-order boundary.
required_components.success_condition: Derive u²(y)=JΣJᵀ under its approximation conditions and retain covariance terms.
required_components.failure_condition: Use the independent-input formula for shared calibration errors or declare the Taylor approximation exact.

required_components.description: Separate Type A/Type B evaluations from random/systematic error terminology.
required_components.success_condition: Explain each information source and attach its uncertainty evaluation to the same model.
required_components.failure_condition: Call Type B subjective error without an assigned information model or equate the two classifications.

required_components.description: Explain coverage factors and nonlinear failure.
required_components.success_condition: Show why a quoted coverage factor needs conditions and supply a nonlinear countercase.
required_components.failure_condition: Treat k=2 as universally exact 95% coverage or ignore a zero-gradient failure.
